heard: A single orbital collision could trap humanity on Earth for centuries. Many believe that space is so vast that satellite accidents are minor, isolated events. But in 1978, NASA scientists Donald Kessler and Burton Kerpale revealed a terrifying reality. At orbit speeds over 17,000 miles per hour, even tiny paint flecks destroy entire spacecraft. If we cross a critical density of satellites, one crash triggers an autonomous chain reaction. This cascading debris storm will continue growing even if we completely stop launching rockets. In 2009, a defunct Russian satellite slammed into an active U.S. satellite, creating thousands of supersonic fragments. This real-world crash proved how easily a single orbital collision could trap humanity on Earth for centuries. You
